page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-2x.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8469C processor operating at 2.6 GHz. System memory capacity is 256.0 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 5.33 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by two GPUs delivering a combined 192 GB of video memory for parallel computation.

The instance features no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block devices for storage operations and operating system hosting. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating network address translation or elastic public IP assignment for external connectivity.

Given the dual-GPU layout and 192 GB aggregate VRAM, the hardware profile favors memory-intensive acceleration workloads over local disk I/O. The absence of local disk requires storage performance to be managed across external network channels. The configuration is aligned with large language model inference, AI model training and fine-tuning, computer vision analysis, and accelerated scientific simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-2x.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for compute-intensive and machine learning workloads. Powered by the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 48 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8469C processor running at 2.6 GHz, alongside 256.0 GB of system memory at 5.33 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is provided by two GPUs delivering a combined 192 GB of high-capacity VRAM. Network communication is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while the instance includes no local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring cloud-attached volumes for data persistence. The high VRAM-to-GPU density makes this server particularly aligned with large-scale deep learning model inference, distributed training tasks, computer vision analysis, and specialized scientific simulations requiring heavy parallel floating-point performance.
